scope.productKind: Node.js software product distributed to customers
covers: Annex I, Part II (vulnerability handling requirements), to the extent a repository can evidence it
Annex II (information and instructions to the user) completeness
Article 14 reporting readiness, as a declared procedure
doesNotCover: Annex I, Part I: product security properties. These are the output of the cybersecurity risk assessment under Article 13(2) and (3) and cannot be established by reading a repository.
Whether the Regulation applies at all, and in which role. Articles 3, 13 and 24 questions are recorded as declarations only.
Conformity assessment under Article 32, CE marking under Article 30 and the EU declaration of conformity under Article 28.

families.title: Components and software bill of materials
Information and instructions to the user

controls.title: The delivered product version is identifiable
controls.intent: Establish which version of which product the rest of the evidence describes.
controls.limitations: Establishes the repository version. It does not prove that the artefact delivered to customers was built from this commit.
expertReviewWhen: the version delivered to customers is produced outside this repository
controls.remediation: Set a version in package.json, tag the release commit, and record the mapping between tag, package version and delivered artefact.

controls.title: Intended purpose and security environment are recorded
controls.intent: The technical documentation opens with what the product is for and the security environment the manufacturer assumes.
controls.limitations: Declared by the manufacturer. Nothing in a repository can confirm the stated intended purpose.
expertReviewWhen: the intended purpose determines whether the product falls under Annex III or Annex IV
controls.remediation: Fill product.intendedPurpose, product.securityEnvironment and product.foreseeableMisuse in the product profile.

controls.title: Manufacturer identity and single point of contact are recorded
controls.intent: Users and market surveillance authorities must be able to reach a named legal person directly.
controls.limitations: Declared. This tool does not verify that the contact is monitored or that it accepts non-automated communication.
expertReviewWhen: the manufacturer is not established in the Union, which engages Articles 18 to 20
controls.remediation: Complete the manufacturer block of the product profile, including a contact that is not limited to automated tools.

controls.title: Regulatory role and product classification have a documented owner
controls.intent: Which obligations attach at all depends on the role and the product class. This tool records the determination and its owner; it never makes it.
controls.limitations: A legal determination. The tool only checks that a determination exists, names a responsible person and is not left as 'undetermined'.
expertReviewWhen: always: this control exists to route the question to a competent reviewer
controls.remediation: Have a competent reviewer determine the role under Article 3 and the classification against Annexes III and IV, then record it with a name and a date in regulatoryPosition.

controls.title: A machine-readable SBOM covers at least the top-level dependencies
controls.intent: Annex I, Part II, point (1) sets the floor at the top-level dependencies in a commonly used, machine-readable format.
controls.limitations: Coverage is measured against the dependencies declared in package.json and resolved by the lockfile. Components introduced at build time, vendored code and non-npm components are outside this measurement.
expertReviewWhen: the product ships components that npm does not install
a bundler inlines dependencies not present in the lockfile
controls.remediation: Commit a package-lock.json produced by npm 7 or later, then publish the generated sbom.cdx.json alongside each release.

controls.title: Component integrity is recorded for the shipped dependencies
controls.intent: Due diligence on third-party components is easier to demonstrate when every component carries a verified integrity hash.
controls.limitations: This control is supporting evidence for the due diligence duty in Article 13(5). The Regulation does not itself require integrity hashes in the SBOM.
controls.remediation: Regenerate the lockfile with npm 7 or later so that every entry carries an integrity field, and avoid dependencies resolved outside a registry.

controls.title: Dependency vulnerabilities are monitored continuously
controls.intent: Identifying vulnerabilities in components is a continuous duty, not a release-time snapshot.
controls.limitations: Detected from configuration files and workflow text. Presence of configuration does not prove that alerts are triaged or that fixes ship.
expertReviewWhen: monitoring runs in a system outside this repository
controls.remediation: Enable Dependabot or Renovate for the npm ecosystem, and add a scheduled dependency audit job to CI.

controls.title: A coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy is published
controls.intent: Annex I, Part II, point (5) requires the policy to be in place and enforced, and Annex VII expects it inside the technical documentation.
controls.limitations: The tool detects a published policy document and wording associated with coordinated disclosure. It cannot assess whether the policy is enforced.
expertReviewWhen: the policy is published outside the repository
the policy must cover components maintained by third parties
controls.remediation: Publish a SECURITY.md stating how to report, the acknowledgement window, and the disclosure and embargo approach; reference its URL in the product profile.

controls.title: A contact address for reporting vulnerabilities is provided
controls.intent: Annex VII, point 2(b) asks specifically for evidence of the provision of a reporting contact address.
controls.limitations: Detects a contact in the repository or the profile. Does not verify that the address is monitored.
expertReviewWhen: the single point of contact under Article 13(17) differs from the security reporting address
controls.remediation: State a reporting address in SECURITY.md or a .well-known/security.txt file, and record it in vulnerabilityHandling.reportingContact.

controls.title: Fixed vulnerabilities are publicly disclosed
controls.intent: Once a security update ships, users need a description, affected versions, severity and remediation guidance.
controls.limitations: Detected from changelog structure, CVE and GHSA identifiers, and advisory files in the repository. Advisories published only on a vendor portal are invisible here.
expertReviewWhen: a publication was deliberately delayed under the justified-case proviso in Annex I, Part II, point (4)
controls.remediation: Publish an advisory per fixed vulnerability, reference its identifier in the changelog, and record the advisory channel URL in the product profile.

controls.title: Updates are distributed through a secure mechanism
controls.intent: Annex VII, point 2(b) asks for a description of the technical solutions chosen for the secure distribution of updates.
controls.limitations: Provenance and signing are detected as textual mentions in workflow files. A mention is not proof that an artefact was signed.
expertReviewWhen: updates reach customers through a channel this repository does not describe
controls.remediation: Publish with npm provenance or sign release artefacts, and describe the distribution mechanism in vulnerabilityHandling.updateDistributionMechanism.

controls.title: Security updates are provided separately from functionality updates
controls.intent: Where technically feasible, a user must be able to take a fix without taking a feature change.
controls.limitations: Whether separation is technically feasible is a product judgement. Recorded as a declaration.
expertReviewWhen: always: technical feasibility must be assessed and justified by the product owner
controls.remediation: Record the release policy, and where separation is not feasible, record the technical justification.

controls.title: Security of the product is tested and reviewed regularly
controls.intent: Annex VII, point 6 expects reports of the tests carried out to verify conformity with Annex I.
controls.limitations: Detected from workflow text. The tool does not execute the test suite, read run history, or judge test adequacy. Passing this control is not a test report.
expertReviewWhen: always, before the result is used as the Annex VII, point 6 test report
controls.remediation: Run the test suite and a dependency audit in CI on every change, add static analysis, and retain the run reports with the technical documentation.

controls.title: The support period end date is stated with at least a month and a year
controls.intent: Article 13(19) fixes the granularity: at least the month and the year, communicated at the time of purchase.
controls.limitations: Checks the declaration and its format. Whether the date is visible at the time of purchase is not observable here.
expertReviewWhen: the end date is communicated in a contract rather than in product documentation
controls.remediation: Set supportPeriod.endDate to YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD and state where the date is published in supportPeriod.publishedAt.

controls.title: The support period is at least five years, or the expected use time is shorter and recorded
controls.intent: The third subparagraph of Article 13(8) sets a five-year floor, with a single exception when the product is expected to be in use for less.
controls.limitations: Arithmetic on declared dates. The reference date is the declared placing on the market; without it the duration cannot be computed.
expertReviewWhen: the declared expected lifetime is under five years
a delegated act sets a minimum for this product category
controls.remediation: Record regulatoryPosition.placingOnMarketDate and a supportPeriod.endDate at least five years later, or record the shorter expected lifetime and its justification.

controls.title: The reasoning behind the support period is recorded
controls.intent: Annex VII, point 4 requires the information taken into account to determine the support period to be in the technical documentation.
controls.limitations: Declared. The tool checks that a rationale exists, not that it is adequate.
expertReviewWhen: the rationale relies on comparable products or on component support periods
controls.remediation: Write down the user expectations, product nature and component support periods that informed the chosen end date.

controls.title: Security updates stay available for at least ten years or the remainder of the support period
controls.intent: Article 13(9) sets a retention duty on the updates themselves, separate from the support period.
controls.limitations: Declared value compared against the ten-year floor and the remaining support period.
expertReviewWhen: update hosting is outsourced to a third party
controls.remediation: Record supportPeriod.securityUpdateAvailabilityYears and ensure the hosting arrangement matches it.

controls.title: The Annex II information set is complete
controls.intent: Annex II is an enumerated minimum. Each of its nine points is checked separately so a gap names the point it belongs to.
controls.limitations: Coverage is measured against the profile and detected documents, not against what actually accompanies the delivered product.
expertReviewWhen: the user information is delivered with the product rather than published in the repository
controls.remediation: Complete the missing Annex II points in the product profile and publish them with the product.

controls.title: Secure installation, update and decommissioning instructions exist
controls.intent: Annex II, point 8 lists the instructions a user needs to commission, maintain and retire the product securely.
controls.limitations: Detected from document headings and keywords, plus declarations. Wording detection is a weak signal and never reaches 'verified' on its own.
expertReviewWhen: the product is integrated into other products, which adds Annex II, point 8(f)
controls.remediation: Add a secure configuration section covering initial commissioning, applying security updates and secure decommissioning including data removal.

controls.title: A cybersecurity risk assessment exists and is referenced
controls.intent: The risk assessment is the document that decides how Annex I, Part I applies. Without it the technical documentation has no spine.
controls.limitations: This tool cannot read, produce or judge a risk assessment. It records whether one is referenced and when it was last updated.
expertReviewWhen: always: the assessment itself must be reviewed by a competent person
controls.remediation: Produce the risk assessment required by Article 13(2) and (3), reference it in riskAssessment.documentReference and keep it updated during the support period.

controls.title: Non-applicable essential requirements carry a written justification
controls.intent: Article 13(4) makes a justified exclusion itself a required part of the technical documentation.
controls.limitations: The tool checks that each declared exclusion names a valid locus and carries a justification. It does not judge whether the justification holds.
expertReviewWhen: always: each exclusion is a legal position
controls.remediation: For every Annex I requirement treated as not applicable, record the locus and a clear justification in riskAssessment.notApplicableRequirements.

controls.title: Technical documentation location, update process and retention are recorded
controls.intent: The documentation must exist before placing on the market, be kept updated during the support period, and be retained for at least ten years.
controls.limitations: Declared. The tool does not inspect the documentation store.
expertReviewWhen: retention is shorter than the support period
controls.remediation: Record where the technical documentation lives, how it is updated on each release, and the retention period.

controls.title: A conformity assessment route and an EU declaration of conformity are identified
controls.intent: Annex VII, point 7 expects a copy of the EU declaration of conformity in the technical documentation, and point 5 the list of harmonised standards applied or, where none were, the solutions adopted instead.
controls.limitations: Recorded as a declaration. This tool performs no conformity assessment and issues no declaration.
expertReviewWhen: always: the route depends on the classification under Annexes III and IV and on Article 32
controls.remediation: Determine the applicable module under Article 32, and once the assessment is complete record the URL of the EU declaration of conformity.

controls.title: The Article 14 reporting procedure is documented and owned
controls.intent: Article 14 applies from 11 September 2026, ahead of the rest of the Regulation. A procedure has to exist before an actively exploited vulnerability appears, not after.
controls.limitations: Declared. The tool checks that a procedure, an owner and a coordinating CSIRT are recorded; it cannot rehearse the procedure.
expertReviewWhen: always: the coordinating CSIRT and the notification deadlines must be confirmed for the Member States concerned
controls.remediation: Write the procedure covering the 24-hour early warning, the 72-hour vulnerability notification and the 14-day final report through the single reporting platform, and name the person responsible.
